question: Behind a sign-up: what does freedns.afraid.org/api/ show a signed-in free account? Third-party client code and guides describe two links, XML and ASCII, to ?action=getdyndns&sha=<SHA1 of user|password>, a listing of the account's update URLs; list every link, action and parameter the page shows, and whether any of them creates, edits or deletes a record.
why: the interface of afraid-freedns rests on no record-management API being documented. The page lands on the sign-in page for a visitor, the Wayback Machine captures of 2010-05, 2014-10, 2019-07 and 2024-03 are all 302 redirects, the listing endpoint answers a placeholder key with ERROR: Could not authenticate., and the acme.sh maintainers say the site offers no API to update records other than the IPv4 and IPv6 dynamic DNS addresses; only a signed-in view settles what else the page offers (AGENTS.md section 2 rule 13: an operator step).
